title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes strict safety standards for AI-powered toys marketed to kids, requiring thorough testing and clear labeling of any potential risks. The law also mandates that manufacturers address privacy concerns, limit autonomous behavior, and provide parents with transparent information about how the toy operates.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act aims to protect children’s personal data from exploitation by AI systems. It sets strict rules for how AI services can collect, store, and use information about minors, requiring clear consent and transparency.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies to submit regular reports on their AI systems, detailing usage, safety measures, and compliance with national standards. The act also establishes oversight bodies to monitor and enforce these reporting obligations, aiming to reduce risks and ensure AI aligns with China’s policy goals.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires AI developers and users to produce regular reports detailing the performance, capabilities, and potential impact of their AI systems, allowing regulators to monitor and assess their influence on society. By mandating transparency and accountability, the act aims to ensure AI technologies are developed in a manner consistent with national security and ethical standards.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act sets out rules for how AI models should be developed, tested, and deployed. It requires creators to be transparent about their models’ capabilities, risks, and data usage, and imposes safeguards to protect users and ensure accountability.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The bill requires that developers and manufacturers of artificial intelligence systems provide a detailed “bill of materials,” listing all components, data sources, and algorithms used in the AI product. This transparency measure aims to help regulators, users, and other stakeholders understand how the AI works and to ensure accountability and safety.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to develop a skilled workforce that can create, monitor, and maintain reliable and trustworthy AI systems. It proposes training programs, educational initiatives, and employment policies to ensure workers are equipped to uphold high standards of AI integrity and safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 sets rules for measuring and reducing the environmental footprint of AI, covering energy use, material sourcing, and lifecycle impacts. It requires developers and operators to assess, report, and improve AI systems to protect ecosystems and lower carbon emissions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 aims to regulate how AI systems affect the planet by requiring companies to assess and reduce their carbon footprints, energy use, and resource consumption. It also sets reporting standards and penalties for non‑compliance to encourage more sustainable AI development and protect ecosystems and public health.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 is a law designed to stop businesses from charging excessively high prices for AI products and services. It also aims to prevent companies from manipulating wages for workers who build and maintain AI systems, ensuring fair compensation.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the agricultural sector, ensuring safety, transparency, and fair access for farmers. It introduces guidelines for data handling, AI system certification, and oversight to promote responsible innovation in farming technologies.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is designed to accelerate the development and deployment of AI technologies in banking, insurance, and other financial sectors. It encourages collaboration between regulators and industry, establishes safe testing environments, and safeguards consumer data while promoting innovation.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is designed to promote the development and adoption of artificial intelligence technologies in the financial sector. It establishes a framework of incentives and safeguards to encourage innovation while protecting consumers, data privacy, and market integrity.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act seeks to boost AI progress by encouraging the growth of skilled talent and innovative projects. It aims to do this through educational programs, research funding, and support for emerging AI companies.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: This act prohibits the establishment of artificial intelligence data centers on federal lands, ensuring that federal property is not used for large-scale AI computing. It aims to protect environmental resources, national security, and operational integrity by restricting such high-energy, high-impact facilities on public lands.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K‑12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 seeks to equip students and educators with the knowledge and skills needed to thrive in an increasingly AI‑driven world. It will establish curriculum standards, provide teacher training, and allocate resources to ensure all schools can integrate AI literacy into their educational programs.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to understand and responsibly use artificial intelligence. It focuses on integrating AI education into school curricula, training teachers, and preparing learners for an AI‑driven society.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed legal framework aimed at regulating the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to ensure transparency, accountability, and safety in AI applications by setting standards for risk assessment and establishing oversight mechanisms.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act aims to guide teachers and students in using artificial intelligence tools responsibly. It sets out rules and best practices to ensure AI is used safely, ethically, and with a clear understanding of its capabilities and limitations in educational settings.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that anyone living near an artificial‑intelligence data center should be fully informed about its construction or operation. They want to give those communities the power to decide how the center will affect their area and to ensure openness and local control.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 is a federal law designed to make sure that any AI tools used in programs for veterans are built, tested, and monitored with strict safeguards for safety, fairness, privacy, and transparency. It requires agencies to create oversight processes, perform impact assessments, and involve veterans directly in the decision‑making so that these technologies truly benefit their well‑being and uphold high ethical standards.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026 seeks to protect people from deceptive AI-generated content that could be used to exploit or harm them. It establishes rules and oversight for AI systems to prevent the creation of false scenarios or narratives that might manipulate or disadvantage vulnerable individuals.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a national program to study how artificial intelligence is being used in court proceedings and to evaluate its impact on justice. It creates a dedicated oversight committee that will monitor AI tools, publish findings, and recommend policies to keep courtroom technology fair, transparent, and secure.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a framework for studying and monitoring the use of artificial intelligence in the judicial system. It requires courts to report on AI impacts, promotes transparency, and sets up oversight mechanisms to ensure fair and ethical use.

title: A bill to require a report on the use of artificial intelligence with respect to access to unminimized information collected pursuant to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The bill requires the creation of a report that details how artificial intelligence is used to access unminimized intelligence information gathered under the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978. It aims to increase transparency, oversight, and accountability for AI practices in handling national‑security data.

title: Decoupling America's Artificial Intelligence Capabilities from China Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: This act aims to separate U.S. AI development from China by restricting technology exchange, investments, and partnerships with Chinese firms. It seeks to protect national security and encourage independent American innovation in artificial intelligence.

title: Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Preventing Algorithmic Collusion Act of 2025 is a legislative effort designed to stop AI and algorithmic systems from colluding to manipulate prices, wages, or market conditions in ways that harm competition. By setting clear rules, reporting obligations, and penalties, the Act seeks to ensure that automated decision‑making remains fair, transparent, and competitive for consumers and businesses alike.
